D008-D001_h004.question_both:
It’s been a weird few months, like I’ve been two different people.

About three months ago I hit this stretch that lasted a good month where I was just “on” all the time. Driving long hauls felt easy, like I could go forever. I barely slept, maybe three, four hours a night, and I’d wake up wired, not tired at all. At home I couldn’t sit still—cleaning the yard at midnight, reorganizing the garage, starting projects all over the place and then dropping them halfway through because something else suddenly felt more important. My mood bounced around a lot—one minute I’d be joking around, feeling on top of the world, and then out of nowhere I’d snap at my wife over nothing. My head felt crowded, like there were too many things going on in my mind at once and I couldn’t slow it down.

Then, after that, I crashed. For the last two months I’ve just felt drained. Even short routes wear me out. Walking up the stairs, my legs feel like lead. Stuff that used to matter—hitting mileage goals, providing for my family—barely moves the needle for me now. Instead I keep beating myself up over small mistakes, like missing a call from my wife or being late by ten minutes. I end up lying there thinking I’m letting everyone down and kind of feeling like I deserve it. It’s made it hard to keep up with work and things at home.
D008-D001_h004.question_a:
For about a month this past spring, it was like someone flipped a switch in my head. I was either on top of the world or snapping at people, sometimes in the same hour. On the road I’d be blasting music, talking a mile a minute on the phone, feeling amazing, then suddenly furious at some tiny thing another driver did. I couldn’t sit still at truck stops—I’d pace, start cleaning the cab, then jump to planning side jobs, new routes, even talking about buying a second truck, all at once. I’d start projects at home too—fixing the deck, reorganizing the garage—never finish anything.

I was only sleeping three, maybe four hours a night but I’d wake up wired, not tired at all. My mind wouldn’t slow down—thoughts racing so fast I couldn’t grab onto one. That kind of hyper, scattered feeling isn’t how I’ve always been; it just slammed into me during that stretch.

Then, after that high period, I crashed for a couple of months. I could barely drag myself to work. Everything felt heavy, like my body was made of concrete. I stopped caring about hitting mileage bonuses or keeping the rig spotless—stuff that usually matters to me. I felt weirdly responsible for every little mistake on the road or at home, like I was a burden to my wife and deserved to be punished for letting her down. It got hard to keep up with my runs and with family life.
D008-D001_h004.question_b:
Ever since I was a kid, I’ve been “the wired one.” My teachers used to say I never shut up, was always fidgeting, jumping from one thing to another. I’d be up late reading comic books or fiddling with stuff in my room, sleeping a few hours and still bouncing off the walls the next day. That never really stopped as I got older.

On the road now, it’s gotten worse this past month. I feel like I’m revving too high all the time. My mood flips fast—one minute I’m joking on the CB, the next I’m snapping at other drivers for nothing. I can’t sit still at truck stops, pacing around, needing to keep moving. My mind’s going a mile a minute, and I can’t slow the thoughts down. I talk fast, jump topics, start three different tasks—checking the rig, paperwork, calling dispatch—and don’t finish any of them. I’ve been sleeping maybe three, four hours a night and still feel wired.

Then, for a couple months before this, it was like the opposite. I was dragging. My body felt like lead, even climbing into the cab wore me out. I didn’t care about miles, bonuses, nothing. At home I kept beating myself up over small screwups—missing my kid’s game, snapping at my wife—and feeling like I deserved whatever bad came my way.
